item.title: The UN Must Protect the Lives of LGBTIQ People
item.description: In January 2024, a father in Iran killed his 17-year-old child, Parsa. item.title: Hotter World, Older Population: How Long Can Climate COPs Ignore the Obvious?
item.description: The world is growing hotter and older. Climate institutions must recognise both realities in whose voices count and where their money goes.

item.title: Gaza winter aid: ‘No more delay’, Fletcher tells governments stalling on support
item.description: The UN’s Emergency Relief Coordinator, Tom Fletcher, expressed deep concern about the deteriorating humanitarian situation in Gaza, as UN member states and partners have been repeatedly delaying sending their support to the Strip.

item.title: ‘Make or bake time’: Guterres urges climate justice pact as leaders gather at COP31
item.description: UN chief António Guterres called for a new global climate justice agreement at COP31 on Wednesday, urging governments to tax fossil fuel companies to help countries bearing the brunt of a crisis they did little to cause. His appeal came as world leaders gathered in Antalya amid unresolved questions over climate finance and the future of fossil fuels.

item.title: From Japan to Rwanda, early warnings are saving lives – but millions remain unprotected
item.description: Early warning systems are saving lives across the globe, but for millions of people the warning never arrives, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said on Wednesday, urging the world to protect every person on Earth by the end of 2027.

item.title: Lebanon: After 48 years patrolling the Blue Line, UN peacekeepers prepare exit
item.description: The situation in southern Lebanon remains volatile and extremely difficult for communities trying to rebuild their lives, UN peacekeepers based there report, despite a significant decrease in hostilities following an agreement in June between the United States, Lebanon and Israel.

item.title: From Nuclear Weapons to Artificial Intelligence, a New Test of Humanity’s Restraint
item.description: At an interfaith gathering in Assisi, nuclear survivors, scientists and religious leaders confronted a troubling question: Can humanity control the destructive powers it continues to create?
